requirement:
Each documented profile defines which grammar nodes are comments; the Markdown
profile's comments are HTML comment blocks, so an inline HTML comment within a
paragraph remains ordinary paragraph text. In every supported language, comments on consecutive lines with no other source
between them MUST form one comment run. A comment that follows other source on
the same line, including another comment, MUST form a run by itself and MUST belong to the innermost outline node
containing that line. Any other run MUST belong to the next outline node that
starts after it within the smallest node containing it; when that container has
no such node, the run MUST belong to the container, which is the root node at top
level. A profile MAY bind a comment kind to its container
instead: such a run MUST belong to the smallest node containing it. The Rust
profile MUST bind inner doc comments (`//!`, `/*!`) to their container, so a
file-level inner doc comment belongs to the root node. Habeas MUST retain the
one-based line and UTF-8 byte column of each inline role’s opening brace or
fenced reference’s first opening colon. When siblings share a line, the
reference belongs to the item owning the comment at that position. A reference
in a comment MUST count for the node its run belongs to under
{cite}`requirements.references.coverage.tests` and
{cite}`requirements.references.authoring_inputs`.
rationale:
structural: `requirements.references.outline_comments` has no implementation edges and no review roots. I found no structural obligation that needs implementation evidence. Each clause describes observable behavior, and a different build would still satisfy it.

- Comment kinds are defined per profile: Markdown uses HTML comment blocks, and an inline HTML comment stays paragraph text. This is a parsing outcome. Any parser or grammar query that gives the same classification meets it.
- Comments on consecutive lines form one run. A comment that follows other source on its line forms a run by itself and belongs to the innermost node containing that line. Any other run belongs to the next node that starts after it within the smallest containing node, or to the container when there is no such node. These rules define the attribution result. A line scan, a tree walk or an interval index would all produce it.
- Profiles MAY bind a comment kind to its container, which MAY imposes nothing to check. The Rust profile MUST bind `//!` and `/*!` to their container, so a file-level one belongs to the root. This is again an attribution outcome and prescribes no type or interface.
- Habeas MUST retain the one-based line and UTF-8 byte column of each reference's opening brace or first colon. This names the information that must be available. It does not prescribe a field or signature. Computing the position on demand would give the same results. Siblings that share a line are attributed by position, which is also behavioral.
- A reference in a comment MUST count for the node its run belongs to under `requirements.references.coverage.tests` and `requirements.references.authoring_inputs`. This ties attribution to those requirements' behavior. It names no library, algorithm, type or delegation interface.

The cited `requirements.references.coverage.tests`, `requirements.references.authoring_inputs`, `requirements.references.source_item` and `requirements.references.test_source_item` supply context only. Whether tests verify this behavior is left to the behavioral criterion.

behavioral: I found no testing gap for `requirements.references.outline_comments`. The tests I read cover each obligation, and every relevant test carries a `{test}` marker. I did not read the implementation.

**Obligations and the tests that cover them**

- **Profiles define comments; Markdown comments are HTML comment blocks.** `crates/trust-but-verify/src/outline/tests.rs#fn[markdown_comments_are_html_comment_blocks_not_inline_comments]` asserts that only the block comment is a comment and that an inline HTML comment stays paragraph text. It also asserts that the paragraph owns the inline-comment line.
- **Consecutive-line comments form one run.** `fn[comment_between_two_fns_belongs_to_the_next]` and `fn[comment_runs_belong_to_the_next_node_or_their_container]` cover consecutive comments. `src/fenced.rs#mod[tests]/fn[comment_fences_close_within_one_comment_run]` and `fn[distinct_runs_with_the_same_owner_do_not_close_each_others_fences]` check run boundaries. Those boundaries are a blank line, an inner-doc to ordinary-comment change, and a trailing opener. All three assert on whether a fence closes.
- **A comment after other source on its line, including another comment, forms its own run and belongs to the innermost node containing that line.**
  - `fn[comment_after_code_on_a_line_belongs_to_that_lines_node]` covers trailing comments on `fn`, nested `let`, closing-brace and closing-mod lines.
  - `fn[a_comment_after_another_comment_on_its_line_forms_its_own_run]` covers a second comment following a first on one line. It checks that the first comment goes to `fn[b]` and the second goes to the root.
  - `fn[comment_runs_follow_the_same_rules_in_every_language]` repeats trailing-comment cases for Python, TypeScript, TSX, CSS, TOML and YAML.
- **Any other run belongs to the next node after it within the smallest container; otherwise to the container, and to the root at top level.** `fn[comment_runs_belong_to_the_next_node_or_their_container]` covers a run before a node, a run separated by a blank line, a floating comment before a `mod`, a tail comment in a `mod`, and a tail comment at the root. `fn[comment_between_two_fns_belongs_to_the_next]`, `fn[trailing_comment_after_last_fn_in_mod_belongs_to_the_mod]` and `fn[top_level_comment_with_nothing_after_belongs_to_the_root]` cover the next-node, container and root fallbacks. `fn[comment_runs_follow_the_same_rules_in_every_language]` repeats these for Python, TypeScript, TSX, CSS, TOML, YAML and Markdown. YAML-specific cases are in `fn[yaml_comments_before_a_key_belong_to_that_key_not_the_previous_one]` and `src/inputs.rs#mod[tests]/fn[yaml_evidence_ranges_follow_comment_ownership_between_sibling_entries]`. The listed languages match the SDK source requirements, apart from plain text.
- **Rust inner doc comments bind to their container.** `fn[file_level_inner_doc_comments_and_unmapped_code_belong_to_the_root]` covers `//!` and `/*!` at file level, which belong to the root. `fn[comment_runs_belong_to_the_next_node_or_their_container]` covers `//!` inside `mod m`, which belongs to `mod[m]` while the following ordinary comment goes to `fn[inner]`.
- **One-based line and UTF-8 byte column of an inline role's opening brace or a fenced reference's first colon.** `src/inputs.rs#mod[tests]/fn[references_in_sibling_comments_on_one_line_use_their_byte_columns]` uses a multibyte `Café` and CRLF line endings. It asserts the one-based line and the byte column of `{impl}` and of `:::`.
- **Siblings sharing a line.** The same test asserts that the reference owners are `Café` and `Two`. `fn[evidence_preserves_attachment_lines_and_declaration_positions]` checks `reference_owner` for sibling structs.
- **A comment reference counts for the owning node under `requirements.references.coverage.tests` and `requirements.references.authoring_inputs`.**
  - `src/rust_coverage.rs#mod[tests]/fn[test_functions_need_a_test_reference]` covers a comment above a test, one inside its body, and closed and unclosed fenced references.
  - `src/authoring/inputs.rs#mod[tests]/fn[references_contribute_their_owning_outline_nodes]` and `fn[direct_test_edges_select_the_nested_item_without_expanding_its_citations]` check that the owning node is contributed.

The remaining marked tests also assert comment ownership at their own call sites. They are `src/structural.rs`, `src/outline_items.rs`, `src/citations.rs`, `src/evidence.rs`, `tests/repository.rs#fn[workflow_job_marks_belong_to_the_job_that_follows]`, and the other `src/inputs.rs` tests.

The optional clause that a profile MAY bind other comment kinds to the container imposes nothing to test.

fenced reference’s first opening colon. When siblings share a line, the
reference belongs to the item owning the comment at that position. A reference
in a comment MUST count for the node its run belongs to under
{cite}`requirements.references.coverage.tests` and
{cite}`requirements.references.authoring_inputs`.
:::{req} coverage.tests
Every {term}`requirements.references.test_source_item` MUST carry one or more
`{test}` annotations in comments belonging to that item under
{cite}`requirements.references.outline_comments`.
:::{req} authoring_inputs
When authoring evidence, the edges defined by
{cite}`requirements.references.roles` MUST determine the reference
contributions to the mandatory input set defined by
{cite}`requirements.authoring.mandatory_inputs`. A `{cite}` made by the subject
MUST contribute the cited definition's complete fenced declaration. A requirement
or example declaration that references the subject with `{impl}` or `{test}`
MUST contribute that complete declaration. For sources outside such declarations,
an `{impl}` reference or `:impl:` anchor alone MUST NOT contribute source text,
except for structural assessments under
{cite}`requirements.authoring.structural_inputs`;
those sources MUST remain discoverable under
{cite}`requirements.authoring.reference_index` and MAY be requested under
{cite}`requirements.authoring.source_tools`. Sources with only `{cite}` edges into the subject
MUST NOT contribute and MUST remain discoverable under
{cite}`requirements.authoring.reference_index`. A `:test:` anchor under
{cite}`requirements.references.anchors` MUST contribute the complete anchored file,
or for a `path#selector` anchor the anchored node.
An in-source `{test}` reference to the subject MUST contribute the source
containing it: for a reference in a supported language, the smallest enclosing
outline node under {cite}`requirements.references.outline_comments`; for a reference in a Markdown requirement, example, or
terminology declaration, that complete declaration; for other references, the
complete containing source file. Literal references, evidence copies, and
generated output MUST remain excluded under the existing reference-discovery
rules.
An in-source `{fixme}` reference alone MUST NOT contribute the containing source
to the mandatory input set. Its acknowledgment MUST instead be supplied under
{cite}`requirements.authoring.fixme_inputs`.
These contribution rules MUST apply only to the assessed subject's direct
references. Including another declaration or source MUST NOT by itself recursively
expand that source's own edges. Reference links MUST NOT be described as proof
that all substantively relevant sources have been found.
:::{definition} source_item
:phrase: source item
A node in a project file’s outline, identified by the project-relative path
and an outline selector. For example, `src/auth.rs#fn[check_token]` identifies
a Rust function. The root node represents the whole file. A reference in a
comment belongs to the item that owns the comment under
{cite}`requirements.references.outline_comments`.
:::{definition} test_source_item
:phrase: test source item
A {term}`requirements.references.source_item` recognized as a test by Habeas.
In first-party Rust sources under {cite}`requirements.references.rust_item_coverage.parsing`,
this is a function with `#[test]` or an attribute whose path ends in `test`,
such as `#[tokio::test]`. This includes functions in Cargo integration-test targets.
